hypothesis: Across exhaustively enumerated families of simple programs, measures of the complexity of a rule's definition are at most weakly rank-correlated with measures of the complexity of the behaviour it produces; some rules of minimal definitional complexity produce behaviour in the top quartile of behavioural complexity, some rules of maximal definitional complexity produce behaviour in the bottom quartile, and a non-negligible fraction of rules that differ in a single table entry differ greatly in behavioural complexity.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Families: (F1) the 256 elementary cellular automata; (F2) the 2187 three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata (Wolfram codes 0..2186). Rule-complexity measures: F1: (a) number of monomials in the algebraic normal form over GF(2), (b) minimal number of two-input gates (AND, OR, XOR, with negation free) computing the rule, found by breadth-first search over truth tables; F2: (c) Shannon entropy in bits of the 7-entry code table, (d) number of table entries that differ from the table's most frequent value. Behaviour-complexity measures: (e) lzma-compressed size (preset 9) of the space-time diagram, one byte per cell, from a random initial condition (width 300, periodic boundary, numpy seed 20260720, steps 200..600 after a 200-step transient); (f) the same for the single-seed pattern (one black / one gray cell, 400 steps, width 801, zero boundary). Statistics: Spearman rank correlation rho for each (rule measure, behaviour measure) pair within each family (8 pairs). 'supports' if max over the 8 pairs of rho <= 0.30, and in each family at least one rule at the minimum value of each rule measure has behaviour measure (e) in the top quartile of its family while at least one rule at the maximum value has (e) in the bottom quartile, and at least 5 % of F1 Hamming-distance-1 rule pairs (1024 pairs) differ in (e) by more than half of the family's range of (e).
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'refutes' if any of the 8 Spearman correlations is >= 0.60 (a direct, monotone correspondence between rule complexity and behaviour complexity) or if in either family no rule at minimal rule complexity reaches the top quartile of behaviour complexity. Otherwise (e.g. 0.30 < max rho < 0.60, or the Hamming-neighbour fraction below 5 %) -> 'mixed'.
interpretation: 'Complexity of underlying rules' is operationalised by syntactic measures of the rule table (ANF size and minimal circuit size for Boolean rules; entropy and non-default entries for totalistic codes), and 'complexity of behaviour' by lossless compressibility of the space-time diagram, which treats both random-looking and structured-but-irregular behaviour as complex (Wolfram's usage also counts class 3 randomness as complex). 'No direct correspondence' is read as the absence of a strong monotone association (rho < 0.3 weak, rho >= 0.6 strong) plus the existence of the counterexamples Wolfram describes. The extension 'and by extension natural systems' is not tested. All patterns are generated by analysis.py; there is no external download.

datasets.name: Elementary cellular automata (256 rules, Wolfram numbering) and three-colour nearest-neighbour totalistic cellular automata (2187 codes, Wolfram code numbering: code digit k in base 3 gives the new colour for neighbourhood sum k), generated by analysis.py with the initial conditions, widths, step counts and seed stated in pass_criterion
datasets.role: the enumerated rule families on which rule complexity and behaviour complexity are compared
